name: Lumino Industries Ltd
title: Lumino Industries Ltd - 544894 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Lumino Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR661 crores, with EBITDA margin at 12.8% and order book at INR2,885 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR661 crores, up 30% YoY from INR509 crores, with EBITDA of INR84 crores (12.8% margin) and PAT of INR53 crores (7.9% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,183 crores (+25% YoY), EBITDA INR155 crores (13.1%), and operating cash flow INR56 crores after paying INR68 crores of trade acceptances from IPO proceeds. Order book stood at INR2,885 crores on 30 September, rising to INR3,093 crores by October, with a further INR555 crores of L1 tenders. Management guided to a 12-13.5% manufacturing EBITDA margin and 13-14% EPC margin, and said debt repayment from IPO proceeds should cut finance cost by INR20-25 crores annually.

financial_highlights.change: stated as 93% in transcript, margin 7.8% implies INR93 crores
INR63 crores in Sep-25 period per Q&A; INR125 crores before INR68 crores trade acceptance payment
down from about 50 days in March 2026

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 manufacturing revenue INR831 crores, 65% conductors and 35% cables; HTLS revenue INR50 crores in H1. H1 EBITDA margin 13%; order book INR922 crores at 30 September, INR229 crores secured in October.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: H1 EBITDA margin 13.5%; order book INR1,963 crores at 30 September, INR157 crores added in October. Revenue contribution about 30% of total, with 3-year execution horizon per management.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA margin guided at 12-13.5% blended; new HT cables expected 1-2 percentage points above normal cables once Ranihati plant ramps, but no substantial margin rise in FY27.
Order book expected to stay in similar range (about INR3,400 crores including L1 tenders, with EPC about INR2,200 crores) through March 2027.
H2 FY27 product revenue expected to rise 30-35% over H1; revenue mix to stay about 70% product, 30% EPC.
Finance cost to fall by about INR15-16 crores in H2 FY27 and by INR20-25 crores annually going forward.
Ranihati Phase 1 adds 10,000 MT; management expects 70-75% utilisation of it in FY28; capacity to reach 75,000 MT by FY28-29 at 80-85% utilisation (56,000-60,000 MT output).
Qualification to bid for 765 kV tenders expected next financial year once six EHV substations are handed over by March 2027.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 40,000 MT at Howrah, West Bengal; FY26 utilisation about 82-83%; H1 FY27 utilisation about 60-62% on tonnage, management says about 80% on value-adjusted basis.
New Ranihati (Howrah) facility adds 35,000 MT in phases, taking capacity to 75,000 MT; Phase 1 adds 10,000 MT.

New medium/high voltage cable facility expected to start commercial production around December 2026 to early January 2027, covering 1.1 kV to 66 kV; medium voltage (3.3-33 kV) output expected from December or January.
Existing plant at 80-82% utilisation, so limited volume growth from current plant; growth depends on Ranihati.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 manufacturing tonnage about 13,781 MT vs about 15,800 MT in H1 FY26, a decline driven by mix shift toward value-added HTLS and AL-59.
Order book INR2,885 crores at 30 September 2026 (manufacturing INR922 crores, EPC INR1,963 crores); INR3,093 crores as of October after INR386 crores of fresh orders.
L1 in tenders worth INR555 crores as of date.
Management sees HTLS TAM of about INR5,000 crores in next financial year, expects to convert 10-15% of it.
AL-59 premium over conventional conductors is modest; margins described as similar, slightly better on AL-59. Conventional conductor demand declining as TBCB shifts to AL-59.

Underground cable orders: about INR50-55 crores of 11 kV and 33 kV orders; about INR75 crores DGVCL (Gujarat) underground cabling order, about 60% HT cable; about INR400 crores of low-voltage cable order book. Management flags price competition as a new entrant in 11 kV and 33 kV.
Exports to 17 countries as of 26 September; UL certification obtained for US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split of manufacturing between cables and conductors, HTLS share, and LV versus above 33 kV cables?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 manufacturing revenue INR831 crores: 65% conductors, 35% cables; HTLS revenue INR50 crores in H1. Medium voltage (3.3-33 kV) production starts December or January; 11 kV and 33 kV order book about INR50-55 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables overdue, collection timing and steps to improve operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors about INR900 crores in March, of which INR230 crores over 6 months; INR215 crores of that realised. Sept operating cash flow INR56 crores after INR68 crores trade acceptance payment (INR125 crores before). Working capital cycle 66 days from 73 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 operating cash flow improve, and from which segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, improvement expected in both segments, mainly EPC via retention money of completed projects expected to return in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: INR264 crores of debt repaid by September out of INR337 crores IPO-funded repayment; INR75 crores balance due 15 November. Finance cost to fall about INR15-16 crores in H2 FY27 and INR20-25 crores annually thereafter.

qa_highlights.question: Will EPC drive H2 growth and stretch working capital? Is 12-13% EBITDA guidance consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Product revenue to rise 30-35% H1 to H2 with 70:30 product-EPC mix maintained, so management does not expect EPC-driven working capital stress. Manufacturing EBITDA 12-13.5% and EPC 13-14% going forward; H1 actuals 13% and 13.5%, blended 13.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Labour shortages in EPC and how addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shortages seen in transmission line work, where the company is not active; EHV substation work uses in-house labour gangs, so labour is not a constraint.

risks_watch: Receivables and EPC retention money (10% of contract value held by project authority) collection timing; working capital dependent on H2 recovery.
Price competition as company enters 11 kV and 33 kV cable market; management expects margins to improve only after about 12 months.
Ranihati plant commissioning timeline (Q4 FY27 per management) and ramp-up to 70-75% utilisation of Phase 1 capacity in FY28.
Volume decline in H1 (13,781 MT vs 15,800 MT) as mix shifts to value-added products; utilisation on tonnage basis only about 60-62%.
Qualification to bid for 765 kV tenders depends on completing six EHV substations (five 220 kV, one 400 kV) by March 2027.
Recovery of about INR2 crores still outstanding from West Bengal Electricity Board, and delays in the Gujarat DGVCL underground order.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and margins, with cautious language on cash flow and new-facility timelines; management repeatedly stressed cash realisation and focus on collections. Several answers hedged on new-entrant pricing and volume growth, and some Q&A responses were unclear due to transcript and audio issues.
key_quotes: So, for us, Lumino is more of a product company than an EPC company, and this is how we would like to grow going forward.
Hemant Bhuwania: So, Abhishek, absolutely you will see further improvement in operating cash flows because our focus is always on realization and reduce the working capital cycle.

adds.what: Ranihati (Howrah) new MV/HV cable facility, Phase 1 adds 10,000 MT (part of 35,000 MT expansion taking installed capacity from 40,000 MT to 75,000 MT)

growth.why: H2 FY27 product revenue guided to rise 30-35% over H1 with order book of INR3,093 crores (Oct) and Ranihati Phase 1 (10,000 MT) starting around Dec 2026-Jan 2027, though tonnage fell and existing plant is at 80-82% so growth depends on Ranihati; no explicit total revenue growth % guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Manufacturing EBITDA guided 12-13.5% and EPC 13-14% vs H1 actuals of 13% and 13.5%, but management says no substantial margin rise in FY27; new HT cables 1-2 pts above normal only after Ranihati ramps, and new 11/33 kV entrants pressure pricing for about 12 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ranihati Phase 1 adds 10,000 MT (part of 35,000 MT taking installed capacity from 40,000 to 75,000 MT), with medium/high voltage cable production starting around Dec 2026 to Jan 2027 and commissioning per management in Q4 FY27; under construction.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 FY27 product revenue guided to rise 30-35% over H1, and Ranihati Phase 1 expected 70-75% utilised in FY28, but H1 tonnage fell to 13,781 MT from 15,800 MT and the existing plant is at 80-82%, so growth rests on Ranihati.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80-82% on the existing 40,000 MT plant (about 61% on tonnage) and the 35,000 MT Ranihati expansion is already in progress, with a further phase beyond Phase 1 implied for 75,000 MT, so a new capex line or phase is likely to be flagged in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book rose to INR3,093 crores in October from INR2,885 crores at 30 September, with INR555 crores of L1 tenders, and management targets about INR3,400 crores including L1 by March 2027, but no explicit revenue guidance raise was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ranihati commissioning slipping past Q4 FY27 would delay 70-75% Phase 1 utilisation in FY28, and EPC retention money (10% of contract value) and about INR900 crores of debtors (INR230 crores over 6 months) make H2 cash recovery a risk to guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Medium voltage (3.3-33 kV) and HV cable output at Ranihati expected from December 2026 or January 2027 covering 1.1-66 kV, with HTLS revenue of INR50 crores in H1 and a TAM of about INR5,000 crores next FY where 10-15% conversion is targeted.

rows.label: Price competition in 11 kV and 33 kV cables
rows.why: A new entrant is pressuring prices in 11 kV and 33 kV, and management expects margins to recover only after about 12 months, against about INR50-55 crores of 11/33 kV orders.

rows.label: Working capital cycle down to 66 days
rows.why: Group cycle fell from 73 days in March 2026 to 66 days in Sep-26, with EPC cycle down to 111 days from 120 and H2 retention money expected back, after INR215 crores of INR230 crores overdue debtors were realised.

rows.label: Finance cost cut from IPO-funded debt repayment
rows.why: INR264 crores of debt already repaid out of INR337 crores IPO-funded repayment, with finance cost falling INR15-16 crores in H2 FY27 and INR20-25 crores annually after, leaving gross debt at INR128 crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book (INR3,093 crores in October), margins and debt reduction, but cautious on cash realisation, Ranihati timing and volume growth, while analysts probed working capital, the 11/33 kV price competition and the H1 tonnage decline.
